summary.headline: Patel Engineering Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 24.5% to Rs 93.5 crore on revenue up about 4% to Rs 1,281 crore; FY27 revenue growth guided at about 10%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue rose about 4% YoY to Rs 1,281 crore, while PAT grew 24.5% to Rs 93.5 crore, helped mainly by lower finance costs (down about Rs 10 crore YoY on lower debt). Operating EBITDA margin improved to 14.02% from 13.4%, which management attributed mainly to project mix. Order book stood at Rs 14,636 crore, with about Rs 9,000 crore of bids under evaluation and a Rs 60,000 crore near-term pipeline. Management guided to about 10% revenue growth in FY27, with most of it in the second half, and said it expects no exceptional items this year.

segments.name: Hydropower
segments.commentary: 68% of Q1 revenue and 62% of order book. Subansiri Lower has 4 of 8 units operational (1,000 MW); Unit-7 concreting started; Kwar dam concreting above 50%.

segments.name: Irrigation
segments.commentary: 15% of Q1 revenue and 17% of order book. Sleemanabad tunnel (11.95 km, MP) TBM breakthrough completed, to irrigate about 2.4 lakh hectares.

segments.name: Tunneling
segments.commentary: 13% of Q1 revenue and 4% of order book. Management expects long-run tunneling mix near 10% of revenue.

segments.name: Roads, Urban Infrastructure and others
segments.commentary: 4% of Q1 revenue and about 17% of order book (balance of order book).

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth of about 10%, with a significant portion in H2 FY27; management cited 15% growth in the following year.
EBITDA margin to be maintained at about 13-14%; management does not see material margin expansion toward 15% given rising competition.
Finance costs expected to stay at reduced levels; PAT growth of about 10% expected for the current year.
Target new order inflow of about Rs 8,000 crore in FY27.
Non-core asset monetization target of Rs 150-200 crore in FY27; Rs 27 crore Telangana land sale completed in Q1.
All eight Subansiri units expected to be operational in FY27.
Patel Smondo OC expected in FY27 after litigation closure; no exceptional items expected in FY27.
capex_capacity: Subansiri Lower: 4 of 8 units operational (1,000 MW); Unit-7 concreting commenced; all eight units targeted in FY27.
Kiru and Kwar HEP (J&K): Kwar dam concreting above 50%; draft tube Unit-1 handed over to E&M agency; Parnai HEP powerhouse roof truss erected.
Dorjilung Hydropower (Bhutan): work commenced in Q1, with potential participation in larger packages.
Working capital needs for execution expected to be met mainly by client advances against bank guarantees or surety bonds, plus possible Rs 100-200 crore of working capital borrowing.
Retention money on balance sheet about Rs 200-250 crore (about 5% of each contract), mostly released at project end.
demand_pricing: Order book 14,636 crore; management expects book-to-bill of about 3x and execution over about 3 years.
Bids under evaluation about Rs 9,000 crore, mostly Arunachal and North-East hydro; near-term pipeline about Rs 60,000 crore. Outcomes of bids hoped by Diwali (per management, tentative).

Upcoming hydro opportunities cited: Kalai-II (1,200 MW, about Rs 14,000 crore), Kamla (1,720 MW, about Rs 26,000 crore), Naying (1,000 MW, environment clearance recommended), Velimalai pumped storage (1,100 MW, cleared). Sawalkote, Kalai-II and Kamla bidding not yet opened; Upper Karnali, Upper Subansiri, Kirthai and Etalin expected this year subject to clearances.
Tunneling: Fotu La tunnel (Rs 1,198 crore) cleared; Mumbai-Pune second expressway DPR (about Rs 15,000 crore) under preparation.
Competition has increased, and management said margins may not expand much; a large project went down last year.

qa_highlights.question: PAT grew about 25% against 4% revenue growth: how much is from finance costs or tax, and what is the normalized PAT growth trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance costs fell by almost Rs 10 crore YoY on lower debt and are expected to stay at a reduced level. EBITDA margin is around 13-14%, so the PAT gain is mainly from lower interest. Current-year PAT growth estimate is about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: Can the existing order book support double-digit growth without material new wins, and what is its execution timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book is to be executed over about 3 years, with book-to-bill around 3x. Target new order inflow is about Rs 8,000 crore this year, needed for 10% growth this year and 15% next year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company have any exceptional items in FY27, after about Rs 150 crore in the last two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not expect exceptional items this year. Last year's items were mainly Vivaad-se-Vishwas settlements and some investment write-downs.

qa_highlights.question: Details of the Telangana land sale and further monetization?
qa_highlights.answer: The sale was 27 acres for Rs 26-27 crore, leaving about 400 acres in Telangana. Other parcels are under discussion. Non-core monetization target is Rs 150-200 crore this year.

qa_highlights.question: Promoter pledge reduction timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoters and the company are in talks with lenders and expect a substantial reduction this year. Management said around 85-90% of shares are pledged and expects at least a 15-20% reduction, without a specific timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Patel Smondo OC timing and occupancy?
qa_highlights.answer: OC is expected this financial year after a pending litigation closes. The third tower is a service apartment tower, ready to occupy once OC comes. Some buyers have taken possession for fit-outs.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins return to 15%, and are buybacks or ESOPs being considered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not confirm 15% margins because competition has risen and a large project was lost last year. Margins are targeted at 13-14%. Buybacks will be considered after debt reduction, which may take two to three years. ESOPs will be handled through the existing ESOP trust.

qa_highlights.question: How much working capital and capex will execution need, and how will it be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Client advances against bank guarantees or surety bonds should cover most needs. Working capital borrowing of Rs 100-200 crore may be needed in between. The 14.02% margin is mostly project mix, with an average of 13-14%.

qa_highlights.question: Dredging, and the arbitration awards above Rs 1,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The company is looking at dredging work, alone or with partners. Arbitrations are being followed up, and settlements are explored where possible. PSUs usually litigate through all courts.

qa_highlights.question: Receivable days and Q2 revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivable days are 40-45, and this continues in new contracts. Q2 is seasonally slower because of monsoon, with some ups and downs but no major disruption expected.

qa_highlights.question: Hydro bids under evaluation and outcome timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Bids under evaluation total about Rs 9,000 crore, mostly Arunachal and North-East hydro, with a Rs 60,000 crore pipeline. Management said outcomes are hoped for by Diwali, which the CEO called hopeful.

qa_highlights.question: Retention money and release timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Retention is about 5% of each contract, around Rs 200-250 crore on the balance sheet. It is mostly released at project end, though some projects allow withdrawal against bank guarantees.

risks_watch: Margin pressure from rising competition: management will not commit to 15% and guided only to 13-14% EBITDA margin; a large project was lost last year.
Execution back-loading: most FY27 revenue growth (about 10%) is expected in H2 after a seasonally slow Q1 and a slower monsoon Q2.
Dependence on new orders: about Rs 8,000 crore of inflow is needed for FY27 growth and 15% growth in the following year, with bids pending and outcomes hoped for by Diwali.
Debt and promoter pledge: total debt rose about Rs 100 crore QoQ to Rs 1,293 crore, and about 85-90% of promoter shares are pledged with no firm reduction timeline.
Pending clearances for upcoming hydro projects (Sawalkote, Kalai-II, Kamla, Upper Karnali and others) and Patel Smondo OC litigation could delay timelines.
Arbitration recoveries above Rs 1,000 crore have no timeline; PSU litigation may run through all court levels.
key_quotes: While the 1st Quarter is seasonally relatively moderate for the infrastructure sector, we remain confident about the trajectory for the year with a large contribution to growth expected in the second half.
So, finance cost has come down during the quarter compared to the corresponding quarter by almost Rs. 10 crores.
We don't see the margins to improve that much.
So, we expect that to come down by at least 15%-20%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY27 revenue (about 10%) and on PAT and balance sheet progress, but cautious on margin expansion, citing rising competition, and vague on timelines for pledge reduction, arbitration recoveries and new bid outcomes. Several answers were given as "hopeful" or "should" rather than firm commitments.
